newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Russia vow to expand strategic ties.
newsitem.headline: China, Russia vow to expand strategic ties.

text.p: China and Russia pledged on Monday to build on their strategic partnership as their foreign ministers met in Beijing, state television said.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen discussed trade and border-related issues during their meeting at the Diaoyutai state guest house, television said.
China and Russia announced what they called a strategic partnership during the visit to China in April of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
Television gave no further details of the current round of talks but diplomats said Primakov's visit was largely aimed at cementing gains made during Yeltsin's landmark tour.
Border disputes between China and Russia have been longstanding though the two states reached basic agreement on border demarcation in 1991.
The two nations share a 4,300 km (2,580 miles) border.

During Yeltsin's visit, China and Russia -- along with the former Soviet states of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan -- signed a treaty calling for all parties to inform each other of the scope of military exercises and agreeing not to attack each other.

Diplomats said Russia could be looking for some form of boost for its struggling economy, perhaps with a new initiative directed at trade. China estimates its trade with Russia could top $6 billion this year.
Primakov, who is on the second leg of a three-day visit to China, was scheduled to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Tuesday afternoon.
On Sunday, the Russian foreign minister made a stopover in Shanghai, China's commercial and financial hub, after arriving from Japan, where he scored a major improvement in relations with Tokyo.

Japan released $500 million in long-delayed aid to Russia while Moscow offered the joint development of a group of disputed islands in the biggest step forward in their ties since the end of the Cold War.
